samples.summary: The behavior half of the issue is not in this change: the promote job still uses the bare `if [ "$code" -eq N ]` chain. The workflow edit ships as an unapplied text blob (docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-workflow.patch), so plan items 1–3 of 20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md (`case` with `*)` default → exit 2, redirect-not-pipe capture into $RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log, verdict-line corroboration for exit 1) are unmet on the branch. The issue's stated outcome — an unhandled status or a node crash can no longer be reported as the benign 'leaving as draft' — is therefore not delivered by merging this diff; only the tests change. Worse, the new test `agent-review-panel.yml handles every mark-ready code, defaults the rest` asserts on the *new* shape and is red on purpose (the todo says 13/14), which means `node:test` in scripts/agent — an enforced lane — fails, so this PR cannot be promoted by the very gate it edits, and if it were merged main would sit with a failing suite until a maintainer hand-applies the patch. If the App genuinely cannot push workflow files, the design-fit answer is to split: land the mark-ready-side mutant-kill tests now (they pass), and keep the consumer-shape assertion out of the suite (or behind an explicit skip that reads the patch/env) until the workflow hunk lands — not to commit a knowingly-red cross-file contract test.

samples.summary: A `.patch` blob is a new, undocumented artifact kind under docs/tasks/active/. docs/tasks/README.md defines exactly two file kinds (`YYYYMMDD-<slug>-todo.md`, `YYYYMMDD-<slug>-lessons.md`) and the generated index only tracks those, so this file is invisible to `pnpm tasks:index`/`tasks:archive` and is the only .patch in the repo (no precedent for this hand-off mechanism). It is also self-rotting: it carries fixed blob hashes (5e4a30189..e2f1304ae) and @@ -1492,16 line offsets, so any other edit to agent-review-panel.yml makes the documented `git apply` fail with no test telling anyone. If a patch hand-off is to be the convention for App-blocked workflow edits, it belongs documented in docs/tasks/README.md or docs/design/harness-engineering.md rather than as a one-off file.
samples.evidence: Glob '**/*.patch' returns only this file; docs/tasks/README.md:12-15 lists only the two markdown naming forms; the patch header pins index 5e4a30189..e2f1304ae and hunk @@ -1492,16 @@.

samples.summary: The harness design doc's 'Ready gate' section documents what mark-ready gates on but records nothing about the consumer contract this change makes load-bearing: the exit-code set {0,1,2,3} with a job-failing default, and the new cross-file requirement that the workflow greps for the literal verdict line 'Not promoting: one or more gates are not satisfied'. That string is now a contract between a script and a workflow (the same category the doc already treats explicitly for HANDOFF_MARKER and disclosure.mjs), so it should be folded into docs/design/harness-engineering.md rather than living only in code comments and a task todo.
samples.evidence: Grep for 'Not promoting'/'verdict'/'GH_MUTATION_TOKEN' in docs/ finds no mention of the exit-code contract or the grep needle; harness-engineering.md:1877-1891 describes the ready gate without exit codes.

verdict.reason: Verified all four legs myself. (a) The behavior half is absent: .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1494-1504 still invokes mark-ready.mjs with no output redirect and branches with four bare `if [ "$code" -eq N ]` tests; a repo-wide grep for `esac` finds it only in agent-implement.yml, shell hooks, and inside the unapplied docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-workflow.patch:47 — so todo plan items 1-3 (case with a `*)` default, the $RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log redirect, verdict-line corroboration for exit 1) are unmet in the tree. (b) The new test is unguarded and reads the real file: mark-ready.test.mjs:34-36 resolves PANEL_YML to .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml and the test at :329 hard-asserts `case "$code" in` (:363), the `*)` default (:369), `esac` (:372) and the non-pipe redirect (:359) with no skip, env gate, or patch-existence condition — I searched specifically for such a guard and found none. (c) It sits in an enforced lane: scripts/verify-self.mjs:160 runs the scripts/agent node:test suite over all *.test.mjs, which includes mark-ready.test.mjs; the todo itself says the test "fails on purpose" / 13-of-14 without the patch (todo:83-91). (d) No hand-off mechanism exists anywhere: the only `git apply` references are the todo's manual maintainer instructions (:76-81). Corroborating rather than refuting, docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260727-scope-review-lenses-lessons.md:8-25 records the identical unapplied-workflow-patch situation and states that design-fit's "deliverable unimplemented" finding "was right". Under the design-fit rubric this is a major/critical spec-conformance failure: the issue's outcome is not delivered by merging this diff, and a knowingly-red cross-file contract test lands in the very gate the PR edits.
